awd_titl_txt: Conference: Student Travel Supplement for 2026 International Congress on Membranes and Membrane Processes (ICOM)
awd_abstract_narration:
This award will provide travel supplements to US-based undergraduate and graduate students to attend the 2026 International Congress on Membranes and Membrane Processes (ICOM 2026), held in San Antonio, TX from July 18-25, 2026. The conference will also offer a student workshop which will involve students learning and practicing various communication skills for both technical/non-technical audiences. ICOM traditionally has participants from academia, national labs, federal agencies and industries. This will provide the student attendees with networking and career development opportunities. Including undergraduate students in these opportunities will integrate them into the membranes community early in their training and career. 

This meeting will cover a broad range of membrane-related topics membrane materials, new manufacturing techniques, a wide range of membrane applications (water treatment, crude oil separation, gas separation, organic solvent separation and bioprocessing) and membrane modeling. The presentations will also include emerging separation areas such as rare earths and critical minerals recovery. The membrane community is focusing on several approaches to improve membrane properties, including new material discovery and design, new and sustainable membrane manufacturing processes and combination of artificial intelligence (AI) /machine learning (ML) and process modeling with experimental approaches. Presentations in this conference will also include “membrane adjacent” topics such as polymer synthesis, advanced manufacturing, and computational material development.

This award reflects NSF's statutory mission and has been deemed worthy of support through evaluation using the Foundation's intellectual merit and broader impacts review criteria.

por.por_cntn:
Overview: This award provided travel supplements to 40 US-based undergraduate and graduate students to attend and present at the 2026 International Congress on Membranes and Membrane Processes (ICOM 2026), held July 18–25, 2026 in San Antonio, Texas, under the theme “Membranes for a Sustainable Future.” ICOM is the premier international membranes research conference, convening once every three years and drawing members of the North American Membrane Society (NAMS), European Membrane Society (EMS), and Aseanian Membrane Society (AMS). ICOM 2026 marked the first time the conference returned to the United States in a decade and was organized primarily by NAMS. The conference was co-chaired by three established membrane scientists — Isabel Escobar (University of Kentucky, water treatment membranes and scalable, sustainable manufacturing), Jamie Hestekin (University of Arkansas, biomedical and biotechnological membrane applications), and Ryan Lively (Georgia Tech, gas separation and organic-solvent membrane materials) — with Oishi Sanyal (West Virginia University) chairing the conference’s federal fundraising committee and student program.

Intellectual Merits: Membrane separations are a key technology for a sustainable future, enabling efficient resource recovery, reduced waste, and lower environmental impact across industries from water treatment to pharmaceuticals. Membrane-based processes can cut energy demand by as much as a factor of ten relative to conventional separations, yet broader adoption still depends on new materials, new and more sustainable manufacturing processes, and the integration of artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) into membrane systems design and process modeling. Unlike region-specific meetings such as NAMS or the Gordon Research Conference, ICOM is the one forum where membrane researchers from every world region convene in a single venue to address these shared challenges and to form new international collaborations. ICOM 2026 program was built around oral-presentation sessions and one plenary talk per day, plus two 2.5-hour poster sessions, followed by a student organized and led professional panel and networking session. By providing a stipend supposed to cover registration and travel costs, the travel supplements were designed to let cost be less of a barrier to the participation of students — particularly undergraduates, for whom this is the first ICOM cycle with dedicated support — in this level of international scientific exchange.

Broader impacts: Funded students gained an international conference experience largely unavailable through other domestic-only meetings: direct interaction with researchers, faculty, and eminent membrane scientists from across the world; and access to potential employers and research advisors from academia, national laboratories, federal agencies, and industry. A student-only reception provided networking opportunities to all attending students (including the recipients) providing a chance to hear directly from experts from academia, industry and national labs. The conference and travel-award opportunity were advertised through the NAMS listserv and the May 2025 NAMS meeting in Tennessee, and by ongoing outreach includes NAMS Quarterly, social media (LinkedIn), and journals including the Journal of Membrane Science, and Membranes (MDPI). Supported students were asked to develop a 3-minute video highlighting their research for a general audience target. These are shared broadly on the NAMS website.
